thread:
maria: Quick heads-up: I'm opening a docs PR to consolidate our guidance on 429s, timeouts, and context-fallbacks. Plan includes updated SDK snippets, a short troubleshooting checklist, and a note about runtime fallbacks.
chris: great — can you paste the snippet you want to replace so we can confirm runtime behaviors line up?
raj: FYI SDK changed last week: retries are now managed via `client.with_retries()` (context manager) in python and `client.withRetries()` in node. Old decorate pattern should be removed from samples.
maria: current draft snippet (old):
```
# python
resp = client.generate(prompt)
if resp.status_code == 429:
  sleep(1)
  resp = client.generate(prompt)
```
jen: also the docs link to /guides/context-trim is moving domains. I'll handle the redirect but pls don't publish the old path.
raj: +1 on changing snippet. I'd recommend something like:
```
# python
with client.with_retries(max_attempts=3, backoff="exponential") as safe_client:
  resp = safe_client.generate(prompt)
```
sam: add a tiny example parsing `Retry-After` header too, teams keep asking how to do that.
chris: runtime note: include explicit line that "if dedicated capacity is exhausted we'll automatically route to compatible model variants in the same region" — platform folks asked for that.
maria: will add. also adding a compact section on prefix/KV caching impacts for context limits.
jen: i'll push the redirect to the guides repo and leave a temporary anchor so the PR can link to a stable URL.
sam: small request: add a checklist at the top that reads: "If you get 429s: 1) check quotas, 2) confirm dedicated capacity health, 3) inspect Retry-After header, 4) trim or cache prefixes" — short and actionable.
raj: note compatibility: the SDK default `max_attempts` changed to 2. Please call that out in migration notes and add a snippet for older SDK users using the decorate pattern.
maria: will include migration snippet and a table with old->new API mappings.
chris: also add a short example for handling timeouts using the SDK's timeout options and show how fallbacks trigger when model variants are used.
maria: adding node + python examples, and a tiny curl sample showing headers:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 3
X-Redwood-Retry-Reason: concurrency
```
chris: can you add a one-liner for ops: "check the console per-route metrics (tokens/sec, err rates) before changing batching/quantization" — ops always asks for that.
maria: will do. PR is up as draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/7042 (labelled errref, 429, docs-sprint). Marking for review after I add @raj's retry header example and @jen's redirect.
docs-bot: PR 7042 status updated to @maria: draft -> ready_for_review
maria: merging tomorrow after final tweaks. thanks all :heart:
